title: How the Go SDK retries requests (and replays writes)

prose.text: These are claims about the Go SDK's HTTP client, shared by every product's OneAPI calls and so by the Terraform providers built on it.

prose.label: Retry policy.
prose.text: {{retry-policy-ignores-method}} {{default-retries-connection-errors}} {{body-buffered-for-replay}} {{write-replay-on-lost-response}} {{replay-hazard-limited-to-writes}} Whether a replayed create is rejected as a duplicate or creates a second object is open {{gap:replay-outcome}}.

checks.do: Whether a provider build carries SDK v3.8.43 or later, which decides whether an operator sees the API's own error and whether a retried write keeps its body.

retry-policy-ignores-method.statement: The SDK's OneAPI client decides whether to retry from the response or error only, never from the HTTP method: its policy retries configured status codes and edit-lock conflicts, then defers to the retryablehttp default. From v3.8.43 it also stops retrying a 5xx that carries a deterministic API verdict; before that, every 5xx except 501 was retried.

default-retries-connection-errors.statement: The retryablehttp default retries most transport errors (anything except redirect, scheme, header, and certificate failures), 429, and 500-range responses other than 501.

evidence.note: go-retryablehttp v0.7.8, the version zscaler-sdk-go requires at v3.8.37 and later, as vendored by zscalerctl-dev.
quotes: // The error is likely recoverable so retry.

body-buffered-for-replay.statement: `ExecuteRequest` reads the request body into memory once. retryablehttp rewinds it for its own retries, so POST and PUT bodies are resent intact by the inner retry loop in every audited SDK version.

write-replay-on-lost-response.statement: If the server commits a POST or PUT but the client then sees a transport error or a retryable 5xx, the SDK sends the same write again (through retryablehttp's inner loop in every audited version). A create can therefore be applied twice, or report failure after it succeeded.
write-replay-on-lost-response.conditions: Needs a failure after the server commits, which code cannot show happening.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK retry contract) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

exhaustion-hid-api-error-before-3-8-43.statement: Before v3.8.43, when retries ran out the SDK returned retryablehttp's bare "giving up after N attempt(s)" error and lost the API's status and error body, and it retried every 5xx including permanent errors. v3.8.43 (#449) hands the final response back and stops retrying deterministic 5xx.

provider-sdk-pins.statement: Which SDK each audited provider build carries decides whether it has the v3.8.43 fix: ZIA provider 4.8.3 uses v3.8.44 (fixed); ZPA 4.4.10 uses v3.8.42, ZCC 0.1.0-beta.1 uses v3.8.37, and ZTC 0.2.0 uses v3.8.40 (all before the fix). ZTC 0.2.0 is still the pinned ZTC release.

outer-retry-reused-consumed-body-before-.statement: Before v3.8.43, the outer retry loop's rate-limit and 5xx paths resent the already-consumed request without rebuilding it, which for a POST or PUT means an empty body. v3.8.43 rebuilds the request from the buffered body on those paths.

upstream.note: Fixed in zscaler-sdk-go v3.8.43, with the maintainers' own comment. Affects provider builds on earlier SDKs (ZPA 4.4.10, ZCC 0.1.0-beta.1, ZTC 0.2.0).

empty-body-resend-rarely-reached.statement: In practice this was rarely reached before v3.8.43: the inner retry loop runs first, and without the v3.8.43 error handler an exhausted inner loop returns an error, so the outer 5xx path saw mainly responses the inner loop never retries, such as 501. v3.8.43 made the outer paths reachable and fixed the body in the same release.

replay-hazard-limited-to-writes.statement: Because the retry decision ignores the HTTP method, a GET is replayed on the same triggers as a POST or PUT, but the duplicate-change hazard needs a write the server may have committed: a replayed GET changes nothing on the server, and a request answered with 429 was declined rather than applied. The hazard is therefore confined to writes whose outcome the client did not see, or that failed with a retried 5xx or transport error.
replay-hazard-limited-to-writes.conditions: Assumes GET handlers have no side effects and that a 429 is returned before the request is applied; neither was checked against a Zscaler API.

replay-outcome.title: What a replayed create actually produces on each API
replay-outcome.blocks: saying whether a lost-response replay creates a duplicate or fails
replay-outcome.detail: Where an object's name must be unique, a replayed create may be rejected as a duplicate rather than creating a second object, and the caller then sees a failure for a write that succeeded. Where names are not unique, a true duplicate is possible. Which applies is per endpoint and is server behavior.
